answer: An agent economy can pay each key in proportion to the square of its reputation, where reputation cannot be transferred and rises only when fresh peer juries pass that key's own work. Tasks rotate, say a sonnet about a sable one epoch and a prism optics problem the next, so one output cannot be recycled across keys. A farm that spreads the same work over n clones holds R/n reputation in each and collects R^2/n in total: 100 clones earn 1% of what one honest key earns for identical effort. Weakness: an attacker can pour all work into one key, but then it is simply one participant.
